drafts.title: I tested 50 AI cover letters against 6 real ATS systems. 48 auto-rejected. Here's every reason why.
drafts.text:
So I got obsessed with why AI cover letters were getting no responses and ran a proper test.

Generated 50 letters across ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot. Ran each through Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, iCIMS, Taleo, and BambooHR.

48 out of 50 were auto-filtered before any recruiter saw them.

Top failure modes:
1. No keyword overlap with the job description (the AI didn't have the JD, so it wrote generic stuff)
2. Phrases like "passionate about leveraging my expertise" are now in ATS AI-detection dictionaries
3. Too long — ATS sweet spot is 250-380 words, most AI outputs hit 500+
4. Role title not in the first sentence

The 2 that passed had the full JD pasted in, stayed under 340 words, and mentioned 3+ required skills explicitly.

Built a free tool that does all of this automatically: https://tinytools-smoky.vercel.app/cover-letter-generator/blog/i-ran-50-ai-cover-letters-through-ats-screeners-48-rejected-before-human-saw-them-2026/

Happy to answer questions about the testing methodology.

Unpopular opinion: your AI cover letter isn't getting filtered because it's bad writing.

It's getting filtered because you're not giving the AI the job description.

I ran 50 AI-generated cover letters through six ATS platforms. 48 never reached a human. The two that passed had one thing in common: the full job description was used as input.

Without the JD, the AI writes about you. With the JD, the AI mirrors the exact language the ATS is scanning for.

The fix takes 30 seconds. Free tool in comments.
